tips.q: How do I write a food photography prompt that looks appetizing?
tips.a: Combine five cues: dish + plating ('on white ceramic'), angle ('45-degree hero'), lighting ('window side light'), texture ('steam rising' / 'sauce drip' / 'crisp edges'), and realism ('photorealistic, food magazine quality'). Steam and gloss are the strongest appetite triggers.

tips.q: Which lighting and angle work best for food shots?
tips.a: Use window side light or golden hour soft light for warmth. For burgers, stacks, and layered dishes shoot 45-degree hero. For bowls, pizza, and flat lays use top-down 90 degrees. For drinks and tall glasses go eye-level to show carbonation and ice clarity.

tips.q: Can GPT Image 2 generate restaurant menu shots with prices?
tips.a: Yes. Quote exact strings (`dish: "Truffle Risotto"`, `price: "$24"`) and limit to 3 text fields per image. Generate at 2K for print menus and delivery apps — the model renders pricing and dish names cleanly without garbled letters.

tips.q: How do I avoid plastic or AI-look in food photos?
tips.a: Add 'natural shadows', 'true-to-life color', and 'subtle imperfection' to the prompt. Include a real texture cue like 'crumb structure visible' for bread or 'oil droplets on greens' for salad. Avoid over-saturated keywords like 'vibrant' or 'glowing' which push toward CGI.

faq.q: How do I make food photos look professional with AI?
faq.a: Five elements: (1) plating ('garnish with [herb]' / 'on white ceramic plate'), (2) lighting ('window side light' / 'golden hour soft light'), (3) angle ('45-degree hero angle' / 'top-down flat lay'), (4) detail ('steam rising' / 'sauce drip' / 'crispy texture'), (5) realism ('photorealistic, natural shadows, true-to-life color'). Combine these in your prompt.

faq.q: What's the best AI food photography prompt template?
faq.a: Reliable template: '[Dish name] photographed in [angle], [plating], [lighting], [color palette], on [surface], styled with [garnish/props], [texture cues], hyperrealistic, sharp focus, food magazine quality.' Adjust dish-specific cues like 'molten cheese pull' for pizza or 'cocoa powder dusting' for cake.

faq.q: Can GPT Image 2 generate food photos for restaurant menus?
faq.a: Yes — and faster than booking a food photographer. Generate at 2K resolution for menu printing. Use neutral backgrounds (white / wood / dark stone) for menu compliance. Our 'Restaurant menu shot' sub-section has tested templates.

faq.q: How to make food look appetizing in AI prompts?
faq.a: Three secret cues: (1) 'steam rising' or 'bubbling' for hot food (signals freshness), (2) 'glossy surface' or 'sauce drip' (signals moisture), (3) 'crisp edges' or 'caramelized texture' (signals quality cooking). Add these to any base prompt and food instantly looks ASMR-level appetizing.

faq.q: Free vs paid AI food photography — which is worth it?
faq.a: Free options (Canva / Bing) generate generic results. GPT Image 2 Studio at 1K (6 credits) gives food-magazine quality. For professional menu / cookbook / Amazon listings, use 2K (10 credits). Comparison: hiring a food photographer = $300-1000/dish. Studio = $0.06/dish. ROI obvious for any food business.
